newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Poll shows growing confidence in post-97 Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows growing confidence in post-97 Hong Kong.

text.p: Hong Kong people are becoming more confident about their future as the transfer of the British colony to Chinese rule looms just six months away, an opinion poll released on Thursday showed.
The telephone survey of 520 people conducted on Monday found 77.9 percent of respondents were confident about Hong Kong's future, compared with 66 percent three weeks ago.
The number saying they were not confident dropped to 9.6 percent from 10.2 percent, the University of Hong Kong survey said.
But another survey, by the Chinese University of Hong Kong, said more of the territory's young people were concerned about human rights and freedoms under communist rule.

That poll, conducted in November and released on Wednesday, showed 26.9 percent of respondents were worried about the preservation of freedoms and human rights after Beijing resumes control of the territory at midnight on June 30.
The figure was up from 17.9 percent in a similar survey in 1995, Timothy Wong, a researcher at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, told Reuters on Thursday.

"If you compare (1996's figure) with 1995, you can see that young people are increasingly concerned with human rights and freedoms," said Wong, who works with the university's Institute of Asia Pacific Studies.

The study, which polled 1,300 Hong Kong residents aged 15-24 from November 3-15, also found that 59.5 percent regarded human rights and freedoms as the most important of all civil liberties, compared with 23.2 percent in 1995.
But 17.3 percent of those surveyed thought the future would be better, up from 12.9 percent in 1995, while 21.6 percent thought it would be worse, down from 22.7 percent in 1995.
"The respondents are getting a little bit more optimistic," Wong said.
Freewheeling Hong Kong has been promised a high degree of self-rule for the next 50 years in Sino-British handover treaties but fears remain over the preservation of rights and freedoms.
